entry.title: Herzog to name Israel’s next prime minister on Sunday, with Gadi Eisenkot in pole position
entry.content:
With 67 of the 120 members of the Knesset behind him, the former army chief awaits the mandate the president is due to hand out on 8 November. In Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp, down to 46 backers, some cry "stolen" election.

After two days of consultations, Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, called the outcome "clear", with 67 of 120 members recommending Gadi Eisenkot against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, but announced on Thursday 5 November that he would keep talking and would not award the mandate to form a government until Sunday. That tally rests on an unprecedented alliance between the mainly Jewish opposition bloc and the two Arab parties: Ra’am, whose leader, Mansour Abbas, says he wants to enable an "emergency government", and the United List, which would back a minority government from outside. In the outgoing camp positions are hardening: a minister from the far-right Otzma Yehudit party told the head of state that the election had been "stolen", although the electoral commission found no irregularities, and the new Knesset is due to be sworn in on 10 November.

entry.title: In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot wins the backing of most MPs against Benjamin Netanyahu
entry.content:
Abandoned by the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party, Benjamin Netanyahu gathers only 46 recommendations, against 67 for his rival, who is backed by the Arab parties. In Gaza, a year after the ceasefire, Israeli strikes still claim lives almost every day.

At the end of consultations held by the president, Isaac Herzog, on 4 and 5 November, 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members recommended Gadi Eisenkot to form a government: the opposition’s 48, joined by the two Arab parties, Raam and the Joint List, with 19 seats between them. Benjamin Netanyahu, whose camp won 53 seats on 27 October, now musters only 46, after the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism declined to recommend anyone without guarantees on military-service exemptions for yeshiva students. The head of state is expected within days to ask Mr Eisenkot, who says he wants to form a “Zionist government”, to build a coalition within 28 days, extendable by 14, with the Joint List pledging to back him from outside government.
